thread:
maya (oncall): 🚨 seeing massive GPU scaling in us-west1, cost alerts firing. Cluster autoscaler is spinning up nodes fast. pods keep flapping in the `batch-gpu` job.
jun (infra): on it, can you paste `kubectl get pods -n training -o wide | head`?
maya (oncall): here
```
NAME                                READY   STATUS             RESTARTS   AGE   NODE
trainer-167b9-xxxxx                 0/1     CrashLoopBackOff   12         17m   gke-gpu-pool-5
trainer-167b9-yyyyy                 0/1     CrashLoopBackOff   9          12m   gke-gpu-pool-9
trainer-167b9-zzzzz                 0/1     ImagePullBackOff   0          5m    <none>
```

sasha (eng-ml): That job is our scheduled hyperparam sweep — we pushed a change to the liveness probe yesterday, could be flapping faster now.
rachel (sre): cloud provider shows node quota nearing limits, also seeing `RateLimitExceeded` on instance create calls. autoscaler logs attached to infra-bot.
infra-bot: AUTOSCALER EVENT: scale up from 12 -> 38 (request: +26 GPUs) reason: unschedulable pods matching nodeSelector=gpu=true
DETAILS: rapid pod creation detected, 95% of pending pods require nvidia.com/gpu
jun (infra): taking emergency actions: 1) cordon `gke-gpu-pool-*` with taint 2) scale down job controller to 0 3) open a quota request if needed. Anyone object?
sasha (eng-ml): do it, please. We need to stop new pods immediately.
maya (oncall): ran `kubectl -n training scale job batch-gpu 0` — replicas scaled to 0. new pods stopped.
jun (infra): cordoned pools and applied taint: `kubectl taint nodes -l pool=gpu dedicated=true:NoSchedule` — should prevent CA from placing new pods.
cloudops-bot: QUOTA ALERT: GPU quota in project redwood-prod-uswest at 92% usage. Request submitted (ticket #INC-6482).
rachel (sre): still seeing many nodes in Provisioning state, cloud API backlog causing long spin-up. need to stop unnecessary VMs to recover.
jun (infra): identified runaway controller: the CronJob `hh-sweep` created 8k short-lived pods due to broken backoff policy. I've paused the CronJob and deleted pending pods matching label `job=hh-sweep`.
maya (oncall): command? will run quick delete
jun (infra): `kubectl -n batch delete pod -l job=hh-sweep --force --grace-period=0` — doing in 3...2...1
sasha (eng-ml): thanks — that was the culprit, our script spawned ephemeral pods per trial and didn't exit on exception.
rachel (sre): after deletes, autoscaler should start scale-down once nodes are empty. set `scaleDownUnneededTime=10m` lower for the moment to reclaim.
jun (infra): changed cluster autoscaler flag to accelerate downscaling and enabled `--max-empty-bulk-delete=10` to remove idle nodes faster.
infra-bot: ACTION LOG: 1) CronJob hh-sweep paused 2) Batch job scaled to 0 3) Nodes tainted cordon 4) Autoscaler params updated 5) Quota request opened
maya (oncall): cost alert suppressed, pending nodes dropping from 38 -> 18
rachel (sre): follow-ups: - create admission webhook to prevent runaway CronJob parallelism > 100 - add ML team alert when job creates > 200 pods in 5m - add test for liveness/backoff behavior in CI
sasha (eng-ml): will add changes to the hh-sweep repo today and open PRs for safer defaults. sorry about the noise :sweat_smile:
jun (infra): we should also add a gating policy: any job with GPU requests > 4 requires manual approval for cron schedule > hourly.
maya (oncall): documenting incident in postmortems and tagging billing team. marking incident as mitigated for now — keeping channel open for follow-ups :white_check_mark:
cloudops-bot: INCIDENT METRIC: peak GPU nodes 42, average cost spike $1.8k/hr, estimate mitigation saved $1.3k/hr
rachel (sre): nice work. final step — schedule a 30m retro tomorrow to lock in fixes.
maya (oncall): will create calendar invite. closing thread but will update if anything flares back up.
